summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on firmware experience building and debugging embedded systems from bare-metal C to RTOS. Programmed STM32 microcontrollers directly against datasheets (GPIO, ADC, timers, I2C) and built FreeRTOS-based real-time control with interrupt-driven peripherals, alongside Jetson-plus-Arduino systems that pair microcontrollers with Linux edge compute over I2C and serial links. Comfortable moving between hardware bring-up, protocol-level debugging (UART/I2C/SPI), and PCB-level electronics work.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system linking a Jetson embedded Linux edge computer to an Arduino microcontroller over a unified WebSocket fabric.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup) for visual servoing and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false positives, servo brown-out, stale frames); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32; implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C and OLED distance visualization; sent control commands from a Jetson-based YOLOv8 detector to the STM32 over UART.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in bare-metal C with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver written directly against the reference manual.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
